-- in --
package main

templ test() {
	<p>
		Text in a template is refilled word by word, but a printer must never start a line with it if you write about it, because the parser would read it as a statement.
	</p>
	<p>
		The same goes for the word that starts a loop, which stays on the line before it when it is for real, and not split from its neighbour.
	</p>
	<p>
		Comments are no different, as text at the start of a line that begins with two slashes is a // note, so it is kept with the word before.
	</p>
	<p>
		A call written in text, such as @home, is a templ element, and the space before it is fixed.
	</p>
}
-- out --
package main

templ test() {
	<p>
		Text in a template is refilled word by word, but a printer must never start a line with
		it if you write about it, because the parser would read it as a statement.
	</p>
	<p>
		The same goes for the word that starts a loop, which stays on the line before it when it
		is for real, and not split from its neighbour.
	</p>
	<p>
		Comments are no different, as text at the start of a line that begins with two slashes is
		a // note, so it is kept with the word before.
	</p>
	<p>
		A call written in text, such as @home, is a templ element, and the space before it is fixed.
	</p>
}
